Senses.Explanation: Before King Awesome Sound: a fixed image of time before received Buddha names and lineages, used to test claims to primordial authority. Yuanwu asks how one could speak its one phrase; Yuejiang claims to have left home then; Huguo criticizes people who presume to belong to that age. Jiqi, Pinjixiang, and Kuifu make distinct present applications to boast, travel, and transmission. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Even King of Majestic Sound did not know; how could Maitreya be clear?
AlternateTargets: The Buddha of Majestic Sound did not fathom it; would Maitreya be lucid about it?
SearchAliases: Majestic Sound King Maitreya cannot know five positions
Caoshan verse beyond ancient and future Buddhas
Senses.Note: Caoshan's five-aspect verse places the line at the final position, where the traces of principle and phenomena are gone. Liangting uses it to challenge a rigid account of reciprocal positions; Baiyu answers a question about what precedes marking; Huanzhu sets it in his own sermon verse. Yongjue later explains the Caoshan verse in this sense. The named Buddhas mark the reach of the challenge rather than a chronology of their understanding.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何履踐？待月來時，與汝相見。第十四則梁山祖意第十四則梁山祖意示眾云：開口道著，舉步踏著，拈在面前，無人能識。搜遠不搜近，宜假不宜真，擔千負計處，還敢商量麼？舉：僧問梁山：如何是祖師西來意？山云：莫亂道。師云：祖意教意，本自無殊。真心妄心，亦不有異。為根機不等，優劣強分。既說淺深，當言頓漸。列門庭，開戶牖，說在駿馬之前。建法幢，立宗旨，獨步劫空之後。曹山曰：洞上宗假，五位君臣。偏正言者，不欲犯中。故臣稱君，不敢指斥言是也。欲明宗要，為作偈曰：學者先須識自宗，莫將真際雜頑空。妙明體淨如傷觸，力在逢緣不借中。出語直教燒不著，潛行須與古人同。無身有事超岐路，無事無身落始終。復作五相。○偈曰：白衣須拜相，此事未為奇。積代簪纓者，休言落魄時。○偈曰：子時當正位，明暗在君臣。未離兜率界，烏雞雪上行。○偈曰：焰裏寒冰結，楊花九月飛。泥牛吼水面，木馬逐風嘶。○偈曰：王宮初降日，玉兔不能離。未得無功旨，人天何太遲。○偈曰：混然藏理事，朕兆卒難明。威音王未曉，彌勒豈惺惺。此頌略分宗趣。西來祖意，豈止一途。派列岐分，應機施設。非刻舟記劍，膠柱調絃而已哉。梁山答處，直截指示。欲使言前薦得，句外知歸。開口動舌，堪作甚麼。未審如何即是。不如緘口退却，與道相應。雖然如是，更須問過監察始得。頌曰：國令嚴嚴擬者危，毫釐纔動鐵輪隨。心萌口應三千里，齒露言來苦怨誰。師云：當頭諱字寰中禁，誰敢依稀犯聖顏？把斷要津，那許汝嘲三攞四？全提正令，豈容伊撥萬輪千？直得慘悚戢翼，內秘外嚴。不見僧問臨濟：如何是吹毛劒？濟云：禍事，禍事。僧禮拜，濟便打。林泉道：賞罰甚分明，若是當時毫釐有差，便見天地懸隔，寧免鐵輪隨來抑逼？金輪王王四天下，銀輪三、銅輪二、鐵輪一。林泉道：若能了一，萬事決畢。四種輪王隨業受報，各具輪寶，摧伏怨敵，雖心萌口應，其奈參差齒露。言時固多利害，何也？但能不觸當今諱，也勝前朝斷舌才。第十五則龍牙烏龜第十五則龍牙烏龜示眾云：把住時放行，維摩一默語如雷；放行時把住，言滿天下無口過。不動唇皮，要通意路，合作麼生舉？還有道得者麼？舉：僧問龍牙：如何是祖師西來意？牙云：待石烏龜解語，即向汝道。師云：潭州龍牙山居遁禪師，因參翠微，乃問：學人自到和尚法席一箇餘月，不蒙一法示誨，意在於何？微曰：嫌甚麼？師又問洞山，山曰

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 如何履踐？待月來時，與汝相見。第十四則梁山祖意第十四則梁山祖意示眾云：開口道著，舉步踏著，拈在面前，無人能識。搜遠不搜近，宜假不宜真，擔千負計處，還敢商量麼？舉：僧問梁山：如何是祖師西來意？山云：莫亂道。師云：祖意教意，本自無殊。真心妄心，亦不有異。為根機不等，優劣強分。既說淺深，當言頓漸。列門庭，開戶牖，說在駿馬之前。建法幢，立宗旨，獨步劫空之後。曹山曰：洞上宗假，五位君臣。偏正言者，不欲犯中。故臣稱君，不敢指斥言是也。欲明宗要，為作偈曰：學者先須識自宗，莫將真際雜頑空。妙明體淨如傷觸，力在逢緣不借中。出語直教燒不著，潛行須與古人同。無身有事超岐路，無事無身落始終。復作五相。○偈曰：白衣須拜相，此事未為奇。積代簪纓者，休言落魄時。○偈曰：子時當正位，明暗在君臣。未離兜率界，烏雞雪上行。○偈曰：焰裏寒冰結，楊花九月飛。泥牛吼水面，木馬逐風嘶。○偈曰：王宮初降日，玉兔不能離。未得無功旨，人天何太遲。○偈曰：混然藏理事，朕兆卒難明。威音王未曉，彌勒豈惺惺。此頌略分宗趣。西來祖意，豈止一途。派列岐分，應機施設。非刻舟記劍，膠柱調絃而已哉。梁山答處，直截指示。欲使言前薦得，句外知歸。開口動舌，堪作甚麼。未審如何即是。不如緘口退却，與道相應。雖然如是，更須問過監察始得。頌曰：國令嚴嚴擬者危，毫釐纔動鐵輪隨。心萌口應三千里，齒露言來苦怨誰。師云：當頭諱字寰中禁，誰敢依稀犯聖顏？把斷要津，那許汝嘲三攞四？全提正令，豈容伊撥萬輪千？直得慘悚戢翼，內秘外嚴。不見僧問臨濟：如何是吹毛劒？濟云：禍事，禍事。僧禮拜，濟便打。林泉道：賞罰甚分明，若是當時毫釐有差，便見天地懸隔，寧免鐵輪隨來抑逼？金輪王王四天下，銀輪三、銅輪二、鐵輪一。林泉道：若能了一，萬事決畢。四種輪王隨業受報，各具輪寶，摧伏怨敵，雖心萌口應，其奈參差齒露。言時固多利害，何也？但能不觸當今諱，也勝前朝斷舌才。第十五則龍牙烏龜第十五則龍牙烏龜示眾云：把住時放行，維摩一默語如雷；放行時把住，言滿天下無口過。不動唇皮，要通意路，合作麼生舉？還有道得者麼？舉：僧問龍牙：如何是祖師西來意？牙云：待石烏龜解語，即向汝道。師云：潭州龍牙山居遁禪師，因參翠微，乃問：學人自到和尚法席一箇餘月，不蒙一法示誨，意在於何？微曰：嫌甚麼？師又問洞山，山曰

Senses.Explanation: The sorrowing person's knowledge of the long night makes duration something known by the one who bears it. Huitang Zuxin uses the line as a substitute answer to how gain and loss are discerned. Yuanwu Keqin pairs the sorrowing person's long night with the resolute person's short day when asking for the phrase of immediate peace. Gulin Qingmao uses the same contrast while commenting on Xuedou's verse. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Entries.SourceTerm: 愁人莫向愁人說，說向愁人愁殺人

Senses.PreferredTarget: Do not tell your troubles to someone already troubled; you may overwhelm them
AlternateTargets: Do not speak of sorrow to the sorrowful; it could crush them
SearchAliases: do not tell sorrow to sorrowful person
Senses.Note: The proverb warns against adding one sorrow to another. Its second line heightens the effect to “sorrow someone to death.” In these sermons it often ends an exchange where a neat verbal solution would miss the person’s condition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 陳明元等請上堂。僧問：「長慶坐破七個蒲團，今日有個不坐底，還見麼？」師云：「鈍置殺人。」僧喝，師便打，僧推禪床，師連棒打退，乃云：「參禪上士，迥脫尋常，鐵額銅頭，頂天立地，巨靈撼而不動，毒鼓檛而不聞，不與千聖同途，不與三賢共住，進一步山崩地裂，退一步雨暗雲愁，有時向毘盧頂𩕳上敲骨取髓，有時向山僧腳跟下剜肉吹毛，不顧危亡，單刀直入，方成個瞎驢種草。倘有人聞恁麼道，便掩耳而去，三十棒賞他。其或未然，必須克勤修證，將多年鐵酸餡咬嚼一番，日久月深，定慧充足，一聞千悟，頭頭物物，盡是自家底，要提起便提起，要放下便放下，受用現成，莫可窮極，猶未可掛放參牌。初學、久參，各宜更進一步。且如何進步處？和煦春風纔入室，炎威又漸逼人來。」下座。上堂。問：「如何是奪人不奪境？」師云：「針峰壓倒阿修羅。」進云：「如何是奪境不奪人？」師云：「蟻口吞乾大海水。」進云：「如何是人境俱不奪？」師云：「一片月生海，幾家人上樓？」進云：「如何是人境兩俱奪？」師云：「愁人莫向愁人說，說向愁人愁殺人。」進云：「向上還有事也無？」師云：「一串穿卻。」乃云：「風動旛動，那堪共語；船來陸來，且居門外。洞山麻三觔，葛藤不少；臨濟乾屎橛，臭氣逼人。趙州喫茶，打濕唇嘴；雲門胡餅，膨脹肚皮。鐵釘飯，木楂羹，梗殺西天老比丘；金剛圈，栗棘蓬，嚇退東土沙彌子。總不恁麼，似覺家風冷淡，且二六時中如何得應用無虧去？」良久，云：「一白缽盂兩度濕，調羹須具調人心。」王氏、陳氏薦夫，請上堂。「綱常，道之基；慈悲，法之雨。雪志守深閨，戒定息繁暑，恬坐一爐香，乾坤闊如許，請余轉法輪，正法無可語，超彼故良人，善處得居處，不圖生梵天，亦不作靈圉，蓮花國土中，菩薩為伴侶，一念已頓超，況對天人舉，樂土本現前，不隔一端緒，閨闈亦可修，晝夜速進取。生滅兩重關，誰是關中主？悟得本來人，非他亦非汝。同生樂土中，長沾佛法乳，諸佛同授記，余門雙信女。山僧無說說竟，諸公無聞聞竟，死者無超超竟，生者無度度竟。且修因結果一句作麼生道？」良久，云：「一超直入如來地，腳踏蓮花步步生。」下座。佛誕，上堂。問：「未出母胎，度人已畢，和尚儼然，將何指示？」師云：「天無私蓋，地無私載。」進云：「世尊出世，度盡眷屬，和尚出世，眷屬還度盡否？」師云：「明眼人難瞞。」進云：「家裏人說家裏話，如何

Occurrences.Kwic: 立，婆云：跂死禪和，如麻似粟。後澄一舉似趙州，州云：我若見遮臭老婆，問教伊口啞。一云：未審和尚作麼生問伊？州便打，一云：為甚却打某甲？州云：似遮般跂死禪和，不打更待何時？婆聞，却云：趙州合喫婆手中棒。州聞得，哭云：可悲！可痛！婆聞，乃歎云：趙州眼光爍破四天下。州聞得，令人去問云：如何是趙州眼？婆乃豎起拳。僧回，舉似趙州，州乃有頌與婆云：當機覿面提，覿面當機󳱈，報爾凌行婆，哭聲何得失？婆有頌答云：哭聲師已曉，已曉復誰知？當時摩竭令，幾喪目前機。師拈云：山僧始者一看，將謂總是白拈賊；及乎再辨端倪，却有浮杯較些子。何故？不因漁父引，爭得見波濤？佛誕，上堂。指天指地，一棒打殺。鴆屎砒霜，合造毒藥。颺在三千世界中，不知那箇親遭著。卓拄杖一下。結制，上堂：西峯結制不尋常，穀滿倉兮僧滿堂，既得遮些根蒂固，大家搖扇取風涼。上堂：門外有一人，用盡機謀，要入入不得。門裏有一人，做盡伎倆，要出出不得。出不得入不得即且置，且道門外人與門裏人相見時如何？愁人莫向愁人說，說向愁人愁殺人。開爐，上堂。三千世界作爐，百億須彌為炭，生鐵鑄就禪和，炙得通身紅爛。正恁麼時，莫有躲得過底麼？左右顧視，云：嗄！將謂水不能溺、火不能焚，元來總是一隊爛額焦頭漢。上堂。十五日已前，󳹸󳹸𣯧𣯧，魍魍魎魎。十五日已後，巍巍堂堂，煒煒煌煌。正當十五日，虗空為鼓，須彌為槌，輕輕擊動，佛祖攢眉。即今莫有解擊底麼？以拂子擊禪牀，云：若將耳聽應難會，眼處聞聲方始知。薦亡，上堂。入我法中，不論凡聖，動轉施為，咸遵舊令，要明少室格外新條。驀拈拄杖，云：未免借伊鼻孔出氣。卓拄杖，云：開甘露門。劃一畫，云：示甘露味，大地眾生頓超十地，惟有今辰覺成上座營齏報薦，考妣二位亡靈不在其內。何故？擲拄杖，云：分明一對黃金骨，不必栴檀入細雕。留兩班，上堂。九旬把定重關，今朝放開一線，頂門具眼衲僧，自合知機識變。乃展手，云：依舊平分局面。復舉：靈雲見桃花悟道：刺腦入膠盆。溈山道：從緣入者，永無退失，咬牙封雍齒。玄沙道：諦當甚諦當，敢保老兄未徹在，泣淚斬丁公。伶俐漢！直饒向遮裏見得，更買草鞋行脚三十年，却來喫西峰痛棒。上堂：一不成，二不是，紅底桃，白底李，紅紅白白不相瞞。因甚達磨大師被流支三藏打落當門齒？通寧智顏菴主送法被至，上堂。裁蜀錦，翦吳綾，披白玉，間黃金。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 陳明元等請上堂。僧問：「長慶坐破七個蒲團，今日有個不坐底，還見麼？」師云：「鈍置殺人。」僧喝，師便打，僧推禪床，師連棒打退，乃云：「參禪上士，迥脫尋常，鐵額銅頭，頂天立地，巨靈撼而不動，毒鼓檛而不聞，不與千聖同途，不與三賢共住，進一步山崩地裂，退一步雨暗雲愁，有時向毘盧頂𩕳上敲骨取髓，有時向山僧腳跟下剜肉吹毛，不顧危亡，單刀直入，方成個瞎驢種草。倘有人聞恁麼道，便掩耳而去，三十棒賞他。其或未然，必須克勤修證，將多年鐵酸餡咬嚼一番，日久月深，定慧充足，一聞千悟，頭頭物物，盡是自家底，要提起便提起，要放下便放下，受用現成，莫可窮極，猶未可掛放參牌。初學、久參，各宜更進一步。且如何進步處？和煦春風纔入室，炎威又漸逼人來。」下座。上堂。問：「如何是奪人不奪境？」師云：「針峰壓倒阿修羅。」進云：「如何是奪境不奪人？」師云：「蟻口吞乾大海水。」進云：「如何是人境俱不奪？」師云：「一片月生海，幾家人上樓？」進云：「如何是人境兩俱奪？」師云：「愁人莫向愁人說，說向愁人愁殺人。」進云：「向上還有事也無？」師云：「一串穿卻。」乃云：「風動旛動，那堪共語；船來陸來，且居門外。洞山麻三觔，葛藤不少；臨濟乾屎橛，臭氣逼人。趙州喫茶，打濕唇嘴；雲門胡餅，膨脹肚皮。鐵釘飯，木楂羹，梗殺西天老比丘；金剛圈，栗棘蓬，嚇退東土沙彌子。總不恁麼，似覺家風冷淡，且二六時中如何得應用無虧去？」良久，云：「一白缽盂兩度濕，調羹須具調人心。」王氏、陳氏薦夫，請上堂。「綱常，道之基；慈悲，法之雨。雪志守深閨，戒定息繁暑，恬坐一爐香，乾坤闊如許，請余轉法輪，正法無可語，超彼故良人，善處得居處，不圖生梵天，亦不作靈圉，蓮花國土中，菩薩為伴侶，一念已頓超，況對天人舉，樂土本現前，不隔一端緒，閨闈亦可修，晝夜速進取。生滅兩重關，誰是關中主？悟得本來人，非他亦非汝。同生樂土中，長沾佛法乳，諸佛同授記，余門雙信女。山僧無說說竟，諸公無聞聞竟，死者無超超竟，生者無度度竟。且修因結果一句作麼生道？」良久，云：「一超直入如來地，腳踏蓮花步步生。」下座。佛誕，上堂。問：「未出母胎，度人已畢，和尚儼然，將何指示？」師云：「天無私蓋，地無私載。」進云：「世尊出世，度盡眷屬，和尚出世，眷屬還度盡否？」師云：「明眼人難瞞。」進云：「家裏人說家裏話，如何

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 立，婆云：跂死禪和，如麻似粟。後澄一舉似趙州，州云：我若見遮臭老婆，問教伊口啞。一云：未審和尚作麼生問伊？州便打，一云：為甚却打某甲？州云：似遮般跂死禪和，不打更待何時？婆聞，却云：趙州合喫婆手中棒。州聞得，哭云：可悲！可痛！婆聞，乃歎云：趙州眼光爍破四天下。州聞得，令人去問云：如何是趙州眼？婆乃豎起拳。僧回，舉似趙州，州乃有頌與婆云：當機覿面提，覿面當機󳱈，報爾凌行婆，哭聲何得失？婆有頌答云：哭聲師已曉，已曉復誰知？當時摩竭令，幾喪目前機。師拈云：山僧始者一看，將謂總是白拈賊；及乎再辨端倪，却有浮杯較些子。何故？不因漁父引，爭得見波濤？佛誕，上堂。指天指地，一棒打殺。鴆屎砒霜，合造毒藥。颺在三千世界中，不知那箇親遭著。卓拄杖一下。結制，上堂：西峯結制不尋常，穀滿倉兮僧滿堂，既得遮些根蒂固，大家搖扇取風涼。上堂：門外有一人，用盡機謀，要入入不得。門裏有一人，做盡伎倆，要出出不得。出不得入不得即且置，且道門外人與門裏人相見時如何？愁人莫向愁人說，說向愁人愁殺人。開爐，上堂。三千世界作爐，百億須彌為炭，生鐵鑄就禪和，炙得通身紅爛。正恁麼時，莫有躲得過底麼？左右顧視，云：嗄！將謂水不能溺、火不能焚，元來總是一隊爛額焦頭漢。上堂。十五日已前，󳹸󳹸𣯧𣯧，魍魍魎魎。十五日已後，巍巍堂堂，煒煒煌煌。正當十五日，虗空為鼓，須彌為槌，輕輕擊動，佛祖攢眉。即今莫有解擊底麼？以拂子擊禪牀，云：若將耳聽應難會，眼處聞聲方始知。薦亡，上堂。入我法中，不論凡聖，動轉施為，咸遵舊令，要明少室格外新條。驀拈拄杖，云：未免借伊鼻孔出氣。卓拄杖，云：開甘露門。劃一畫，云：示甘露味，大地眾生頓超十地，惟有今辰覺成上座營齏報薦，考妣二位亡靈不在其內。何故？擲拄杖，云：分明一對黃金骨，不必栴檀入細雕。留兩班，上堂。九旬把定重關，今朝放開一線，頂門具眼衲僧，自合知機識變。乃展手，云：依舊平分局面。復舉：靈雲見桃花悟道：刺腦入膠盆。溈山道：從緣入者，永無退失，咬牙封雍齒。玄沙道：諦當甚諦當，敢保老兄未徹在，泣淚斬丁公。伶俐漢！直饒向遮裏見得，更買草鞋行脚三十年，却來喫西峰痛棒。上堂：一不成，二不是，紅底桃，白底李，紅紅白白不相瞞。因甚達磨大師被流支三藏打落當門齒？通寧智顏菴主送法被至，上堂。裁蜀錦，翦吳綾，披白玉，間黃金。

Senses.Explanation: Do not tell your troubles to someone already troubled; you may overwhelm them turns a common warning into a refusal of easy talk. Tian’an says it after imagining the monastery’s food running out and offering an ancestral substitute. Baichi quotes it after a funeral story and then asks what the mourners actually understood. Eryin uses it as the answer to an imagined challenge about why grief remains after understanding. Chaozong ends a sermon with it after criticizing dry, secondhand understanding. Lianfeng uses it to answer one of the four questions about person and setting. Gaofeng speaks it in a hall address after asking how a person outside and a person inside could meet.

Senses.Explanation: Fazhou Ji uses the saying to cap the shared grief of grave-side mourners; Chaozong and Gaofeng place it in exchanges where one troubled position cannot free another. At the graveside Fazhou sets public festivity against lamentation before giving the line. Chaozong records his own rejected answer with it; Gaofeng puts it between the person unable to enter and the person unable to leave.

Senses.Explanation: Keeping precepts enters these records as instruction, remembered practice, and an object of Chan questioning. In a short instruction to the nun Jianwei, Poshan Haiming contrasts a precept keeper who does not ascend to heaven with a violator who does not fall into hell. He then says understanding that point enables genuine precept keeping; the term is part of his challenge to a simple reward-and-punishment reading. In a hall sermon, Changmu Guangdian tells of a strict precept keeper who fears he crushed a pregnant frog at night and dreams of accusing frogs. Senses.Note: The paired statement questions the sufficiency of outward restraint while its surrounding passages continue to demand practice and responsible conduct. Received scripture citations change the primary verse wording from keeping and violating to keeping precepts; the primary named speaker is not thereby the exact utterer of the altered words.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan. Poshan Haiming addresses the precept recipient Kongru with the pair, then calls it the point of the monk's precepts. He objects that people instead locate precepts entirely in their three robes and bowl, and says this fails both the earlier sages and oneself. His final question asks how carrying a pig's head while keeping pure precepts, or taking dog bones into a brothel, could be understood. These deliberately difficult images challenge identifying restraint with its outward equipment; they do not turn the passage into permission to harm or exploit others.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan. Addressing the precept recipient Yinxi, Poshan Haiming calls the pair the substance of precepts, but immediately says that the six kinds of cultivation and myriad practices are cultivated and verified from here. He adds that cultivation and verification are possible while defilement is inadmissible, then asks what it is that is not defiled. The apparent limit on bodily restraint opens an inquiry into its basis. The following insistence on practice prevents reading the pair as a declaration that keeping precepts is simply unnecessary.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB208.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhe. Guxue Zhenzhe criticizes two opposed evasions. Those who quote Huineng to excuse drinking, eating meat and dismissing consequences mistake words addressed to a particular occasion; those who cling only to robes and bowl mistake the remedy for a disease. He gives the pair against the latter, while explicitly saying that understanding the emptiness of wrongdoing does not mean committing harmful acts and that even a small good is not to be slighted. The bodily limit checks the sufficiency of outward observance without endorsing the conduct criticized on the other side.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB208.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhe. Guxue Zhenzhe records a visitor arriving before the winter month begins and asking for precepts. Speaking under his self-designation Ordinary Man, Guxue responds with the pair and asks what benefit such a request has. The visitor answers that precepts are the basis for Chan and Chan their culmination, and hopes to leave hired ritual work with neighboring practitioners. Guxue then praises this intention and encourages the combination of precepts, Chan and benefiting oneself and others. Senses.Explanation: The pair limits what outward precept-keeping can settle and turns the hearer toward the body, its assumed boundaries, and the basis of conduct. Its Chan uses question the sufficiency of bodily restraint while repeatedly preserving the demand for practice and responsibility. Poshan Haiming addresses the precept recipient Kongru with the pair, then calls it the point of the monk's precepts. He objects that people instead locate precepts entirely in their three robes and bowl, and says this fails both the earlier sages and oneself. His final question asks how carrying a pig's head while keeping pure precepts, or taking dog bones into a brothel, could be understood. These deliberately difficult images challenge identifying restraint with its outward equipment; they do not turn the passage into permission to harm or exploit others. Addressing the precept recipient Yinxi, Poshan Haiming calls the pair the substance of precepts, but immediately says that the six kinds of cultivation and myriad practices are cultivated and verified from here. He adds that cultivation and verification are possible while defilement is inadmissible, then asks what it is that is not defiled. The apparent limit on bodily restraint opens an inquiry into its basis. The following insistence on practice prevents reading the pair as a declaration that keeping precepts is simply unnecessary. Guxue Zhenzhe criticizes two opposed evasions. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. Chushi Fanqi raises the six recollections named in scripture: Buddha, teaching, community, precepts, heaven and giving. He asks what a monk should recollect, then blocks each ready-made answer with a saying. For recollecting precepts he gives the complete body-and-binding pair and says that this cannot be recollection of precepts. After similarly rejecting the other labels, he asks whether the answer is no thought, only to say that as soon as one makes it no thought it has become a thought: escaping drowning has led into fire. Even claiming to stand alone without dependence, he says, would not qualify one as a monk's servant. The headword is inherited textual wording in this present challenge, not a definition Chushi supplies as the final answer. Its local function is to stop the assembly from resting in the label of precepts or its simple negation. The retained frame supplies no personal name for the earlier scriptural voice.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如是，且道：老僧恁麼道，與從上百二十院老古錐說底相去幾何？良久，云：落霞與孤鶩齊飛，秋水共長天一色。怡然、若松二上座請上堂。人間花甲子，世相妄推遷，一句為君盡，剎那是大年。所以三世諸佛、歷代祖師以及天下老和尚，盡在剎那際裏說法利生，至今猶未起在。只如剎那義作麼生商量？知麼？纔生不可得，不貴未生前。溫陵慈門上人請上堂，僧問：昔日花開即不問，今朝果熟事如何？師云：果在什麼處？進云：唯此一事實，餘二則非真。師云：猶未熟在。僧問：雪覆千山，為甚麼孤峯不白？師云：不與眾同流。僧禮拜，師拈拄杖云：日日釋迦出世，時時彌勒誕生，且道這箇木上座幾時出世？幾時誕生？良久，云：常在闤闠中，從來不合伴。卓一卓，云：珍重！實彩上人請上堂。古教道：一切法不生，一切法不滅，若能如是解，諸佛常現前。鼓山則不然，諸法念念生，諸法念念滅，若能如是解，諸佛常現前。大眾！古教教人於不生滅處見佛，鼓山教人於生滅處見佛，且道：生滅與不生不滅是同？是別？良久，云：空外之青山善走，江間之白浪不流。下座。同參上人請上堂：有相身中無相身，謾將歲月較疎親，直饒八萬四千劫，子細看來過隙塵。雖然如是，只如今日同參上人遠來設供慶讚一句作麼生？金果早朝猿摘去，玉花晚後鳳啣來。慈門上人領眾求戒，請上堂。大眾遠來求戒，為壇塲是戒耶？問清淨是戒耶？三說羯磨是戒耶？乃至教威儀、著袈裟、乞食是戒耶？喝一喝，云：是非已去了，是非裏薦取。懸鏡上人領眾求戒，請上堂。戒性如虗空，持者為迷倒。若人會得如空戒性，則知威音王已前受戒竟，不假三師羯磨，何煩七證揀非？如或未然，細刮龜毛搓索子，緊把虗空縛一場，直待通身流白汗，方如好肉本無瘡。德淡上人領眾求戒，請上堂。持犯但束身，非身無所束。如何是身？如何是非身？身與非身，是一？是二？豈不見釋迦老子道：如來所說身相即非身相。如是，則如來所說戒相即非戒相。受者，如是而受，受無所受；持者，如是而持，持無所持。五篇七聚，無非文殊玅門；著衣展鉢，盡是舍那心地。還有恁麼人麼？若有，堪報不報之恩，足了未了之事，令法久住壽佛慧命；如或未然，且教順朱去。梵音、忍茂二上人求戒，請上堂。人人有箇本源自性清淨戒，圓滿具足，無欠無餘，逼塞虗空，充滿正報。且道箇中誰受？誰學？誰修？誰證？大眾知麼？自𢹂瓶去沽村酒，又著衫來作主人。同參上人領眾求戒，請上堂。僧問：戒性人人本有，為甚麼又要受戒？師云：若不受戒，焉知本有？進云：恁麼則龜毛索子緊縛虗空去也。師云：汝還縛得著麼？僧擬議，師便打。乃卓拄杖，云：天人羣生類，皆承此恩力。且道此是甚麼？若喚作佛，相好難形；喚作法，詮顯不出；喚作僧，非和合相；喚作戒，無非可防。且道畢竟是箇甚麼？良久，云：野老不知堯舜力，鼕鼕打鼓祭江神。又卓一卓，下座。性空、性質、寂理三位上人領眾求戒，請上堂。昔日先師老和尚開戒，親垂三問，當時答者固多，契機者少。滅度以來已三十載，此問鮮有知之者，今日不免為大眾從頭舉出，一以供養先師，一令人人知有。第一問：戒必師師相授，且道威音王從何人受戒？著語云：石女親開口，羯磨不登壇。第二問：戒光從口出，非青黃赤白，畢竟作何色？著語云：本光瑞如此，莫向色邊求。第三問：破戒比丘為甚麼不墮地獄？著語云：十界無安處，他得大闡提。大眾！問在答處？答在問處？先師問底即是霈上座答底，霈上座答底即是先師問底。若向這裏直下徹去，方知先師老人常住此山，未曾滅度，實無一時、無一處、無一事不為諸人

At a hall address requested by Dedan and others seeking precepts, Weilin Daopei opens with the same pair, then asks what body is, what nonbody is, and whether body and nonbody are one or two. He cites Shakyamuni's saying that the body's form is not body-form, and applies the same questioning to the form of precepts. Receiving is to be done without taking possession of a received thing, and keeping without possession of a keeper's accomplishment. He then brings the categories of rules together with putting on the robe and opening the bowl as occasions of this teaching. Asking whether anyone can live this way, he says such a person can repay the unrepayable kindness and keep the teaching alive; otherwise one should follow the model for now. The old pair therefore opens an actual precept-request assembly and a set of questions about receiving and keeping, rather than cancelling everyday conduct. The locally named Shakyamuni belongs to the following body-form saying; the opening clause itself is not assigned an original personal speaker by the record.

Senses.Explanation: Keeping and breaking precepts bind only the body; what is not body cannot be bound. Chushi Fanqi raises the six recollections named in scripture: Buddha, teaching, community, precepts, heaven and giving. He asks what a monk should recollect, then blocks each ready-made answer with a saying. For recollecting precepts he gives the complete body-and-binding pair and says that this cannot be recollection of precepts. After similarly rejecting the other labels, he asks whether the answer is no thought, only to say that as soon as one makes it no thought it has become a thought: escaping drowning has led into fire. Even claiming to stand alone without dependence, he says, would not qualify one as a monk's servant. Entries.SourceTerm: 漁歌驚起沙汀鷺，飛出蘆花不見蹤

Senses.PreferredTarget: A fisherman's song startles egrets on the sandbar; they fly into the reeds and vanish without a trace
AlternateTargets: The fisherman's song flushes the shore egrets, which disappear into the reed blossoms
SearchAliases: fisher song egrets reeds vanish Chan
sandbar egret reed blossoms noble route Zen
Senses.Note: Asked about the noble route, Xueting answers with a fisherman's song that sends sandbar egrets into the reeds until they disappear. Buhui revoices the pair to answer a fresh request for face-to-face discernment. Sanyi, Liangting, and Zhe'an each quote Xueting's old answer and give a distinct present comment on what the respondent or observer misses. The sudden vanishing matters as much as the bird or the song.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 月十九，耳聾眼瞎獻醜，遍界鳥啼花笑，青山綠水伸手，觀音玅相全彰，人人各自抖擻，一段親切家常，這樣誰家不有？更問祖意西來，天地壞時不朽，應化萬般一貫，仰高彌堅非首，出沒充滿太虛，彌雲普覆星斗。碧山看來，大似春眠不覺曉，處處聞啼鳥，夜來風雨聲，花落知多少？」驀豎杖，云：「觀音菩薩在拄杖頭上說法已竟，諸人有眼皆見、有耳共聞，既見、既聞，天下無二道、聖人無兩心。所以，或現帝王身說法、或現宰官身說法、或現將軍身說法、或現比丘身隨類說法。且道：即今觀音畢竟在甚麼處？」復一喝：「一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私？」拍禪床，下座。何其高為剃僧設齋，請上堂。僧問：「前無輕遮，後無重難，寸絲不挂，還有戒受否？」師云：「一刀截斷兩頭空。」進云：「舉頭盡是目前意，鼻直露出頂中圓。」師云：「星光獨耀無遮覆，盡虛空界秪一人。」進云：「青山常不動，旋繞玉麒麟，如何是麒麟主？」師云：「突出難辨。」僧問：「許多家常不辦事，相逢覿面目難開，望和尚洞察其情。」師云：「漁歌驚起沙汀鷺，飛出蘆花不見蹤。」進云：「曠劫盡成羅剎漢，今朝鐵額又相逢，未審是甚麼物？」師云：「漢地不收秦不管。」進云：「乞和尚瓦解冰消。」師一喝連打。僧問：「臘月八，我佛成道，還有人成道否？」師云：「誰家灶裏無煙火？」進云：「禪和不開口，諸佛難下手，如何是下手處？」師高聲云：「是真下手。」進云：「舉一口無底缽如何受持？」師云：「大家在裏許。」進云：「一口氣不來，缽在甚處？」師云：「普。」乃云：「多時不上堂，滿肚無一字。受新戒沙彌，兩腳踏實地，勿隨五欲染，當頭直切去，如自守孤城，不容煙塵聚。本體如虛空，雲霞似戒衣，不住持犯戒，方堪出家兒。」復舉：「戒云：『戒戒戒，這段家常非內外；衣衣衣，玉兔金烏難繫拘；持持持，兔角龜毛等不齊。』若向此薦得，六祖云：『心地無非自性戒，心地無亂自性定，心地無癡自性慧。』眾生受此戒，即入諸佛位。重示一偈：戒相如空強作持，明明不薦弄花枝，尋常契合虛玄玅，遍界無非一坐具。」為見空監院對靈上堂。師以拂子打○相云：「見空見色非眼見，今朝與公通一線，踏碎煙塵日轉西，大似長空收過電。明暗盡時一顆寒，有見無見俱坐斷。既是俱坐斷，且道見空監院在甚處一喝？處處林泉堪寄馬，明明獨耀個郎當。個郎當，人歸算子水歸江，智光迥迥射寒窗。」為常鼎懺罪，請

Senses.Explanation: A fisherman, often deployed as a literary figure with boat, line, flute, song, and water. The Chan corpus gives the type several jobs rather than one abstract interpretation. In the Linked Lamps Compendium Cuiyan Kezhen calls entering dragon-filled water the fisherman's courage, asks what a patch-robed monk's courage is, and raises the staff. In the Five Lamps Complete Collection Huitang Zuxin threatens to take the fisherman's flute and play by the sea if nobody can determine the currents. At an installation Wushan Jingduan sings one fisherman's song, calls it a song of peace, and mounts the seat. Tianyin Yuanxiu says that without a fisherman leading one cannot see the waves, while Jiashan Shanhui demands that a sword be wielded lest the fisherman nest. These public questions, staff actions, seat opening, guidance, and deliberately impossible nesting are Chan uses of the fisherman type.

SearchAliases: the Fisherman in the Qu Yuan dialogue
Zen the Fisherman in the Qu Yuan dialogue
Senses.Explanation: The Fisherman who meets Qu Yuan is an identifiable classical dialogue figure. Wansong's commentary supplies the encounter background: the exiled Qu Yuan walks by the river and tells the Fisherman that the whole world is drunk while he alone is sober and that everyone is muddy while he alone is clear. Elsewhere Wansong quotes the Fisherman's clear-water and muddy-water song. A later Chan verse names Qu Yuan and the Fisherman together, declares both wrong, sends each home with his own song, and redirects the pair toward a road through the gate of birth and death. The corpus therefore does more than use a generic occupation here: it repeatedly recalls the same paired literary encounter and then appraises both participants from within Chan verse.

Senses.Explanation: Fisherman also occurs as the exact title of a work or poem, a different lexical object from the person it depicts. One prose passage names Fisherman among Qu Yuan's works and says he used it to give himself release. Independent Chan collections place the bare word in section headings above poems: one poem describes moonlight, reed flowers, a fishing boat, dangerous waves, and a cormorant; another describes years passed in a skiff and a fisherman's flute at dusk; a third describes a fishing boat, a thousand-foot line held within a square inch, and the search for a giant fish. Larger titles such as Fisherman's Song belong to the same title family but are not required to establish that the bare headword itself names written works.

HeadwordSpanReview.GrammarEvidence: Tian’an Sheng deliberately repeats 省悟 across contrasting categories in one uninterrupted address.

Senses.Explanation: To come to understand is to awaken to the matter rather than merely acquire information. In the wash-your-bowl case, the narrator marks the event with 忽然: the monk suddenly comes to understand after Zhaozhou’s answer. Foyan turns attention from the label to 省悟之由, the basis or occasion of understanding, and warns against stopping after grasping a few sayings. Tian’an applies the term across monks and laypeople, sages and ordinary people, the wise and foolish, then asks whether anyone present has not understood. Suddenness and occasion belong to particular contexts; they do not create separate lexical senses.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase ‘Old monk’ is both an ordinary designation for an elderly monk and the conventional first-person self-reference used by named teachers such as Baizhang Huaihai, Linji Yixuan, Zhaozhou Congshen, and Yunju Daoqi. The human role remains the same across narration, address, and self-reference; those grammatical settings do not create separate senses. Its characteristic Chan use is humble first-person self-reference in monastic speech, conventionally translated ‘this old monk’ and grammatically serving as ‘I’ or ‘me.’ Baizhang Huaihai recalls receiving Mazu Daoyi’s shout; Linji Yixuan says he sits securely and distinguishes the visitors who come; Zhaozhou Congshen redirects a public interview by saying, ‘this old monk is hard of hearing; ask loudly’; and Yunju Daoqi addresses the assembly at his final meeting. The same noun phrase also refers in narration to an old monk: Wuzhuo meets one, a raised case begins with an old monk carried by two disciples, and a record introduces ‘an old monk named Puhui.’ Speaker self-reference, third-person reference, and definiteness are contextual readings of the same human-role noun, not different things.

Entries.SourceTerm: 老僧二十年前有老婆心，二十年後無老婆心

Senses.PreferredTarget: Twenty years ago this old monk had kindly concern; twenty years later he had none
AlternateTargets: Twenty years ago I had grandmotherly concern; twenty years later I no longer did
SearchAliases: Jinfeng twenty years kindly concern before after
grandmotherly concern twenty years JinFeng Chan
Senses.Note: Jinfeng says he had kindly concern twenty years earlier and none twenty years later. In the case he explains the earlier period as answering ordinary and sacred questions in kind, and the later period as refusing that matching answer. Tianyin challenges an inherited judgment, Tian'an and Baiyu reverse the timing, Zhe'an questions the response pattern, and Hansong rejects both sides. Their current uses make the line a test of care in the actual encounter, not a biography of changing temperament.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Master Ma's shout left me deaf for three days
SearchAliases: master ma's shout left me deaf for three days
Senses.Note: Baizhang Huaihai reports that a shout from his teacher Mazu left him deaf for three days. When Huangbo hears this, he sticks out his tongue, and Baizhang asks whether he plans to inherit Mazu's way. Sanyi weighs old explanations that either dismiss or depend on the three days of deafness. Jie'an places the report beside Mazu's original shout and composes a verse about its dangerous force. Hanyue asks how the great function in the encounter can be recognized; Neishao composes verses that take both Baizhang's recollection and Huangbo's startled response as part of the test. The sentence names a particular encounter and its delayed effect, not a general rule about shouting.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 老僧罪過 says that 'this old monk is at fault.' In Chan dialogue it is a compact response whose force depends on the preceding turn. Master Yi uses it after receiving a pointed answer; Xinghua presents it as the capping reply that covers Linji's staged 'new arrival'; and Mazu returns Baizhang's own admission of fault. The phrase can accept, cap, or turn fault-language without naming a concrete offense, but these pragmatic uses all retain the same first-person self-reference and do not warrant separate senses.

Senses.Explanation: The epithet pictures a seasoned Chan figure as an “old awl”: pointed, penetrating, and difficult to blunt. A Linked Pearls verse applies it teasingly to the Buddha, while Baoshou Fang speaks of deceiving the old awls of past generations. Xitai Qibian turns the phrase against an earlier master, Feiyin Tongrong groups famous old teachers as a whole company of old awls, and Yinyuan Longqi theatrically says that casting down his staff releases a company of them. Juelang Daosheng submits a whole company of sharp old figures to renewed judgment.

Senses.Explanation: Grandmotherly concern is an elder’s solicitous willingness to explain, protect, or labour for someone even at the risk of being called overindulgent. Linji recognizes Huangbo’s repeated blows as such concern; commentators apply it to a protecting phrase or to inherited explanations, sometimes gratefully and sometimes as criticism for entering the mud. The local verdict controls the tone.

AlternateTargets: old-woman concern pressed to the utmost

Senses.Note: The phrase is neither automatically praise nor a guarantee that the action described is harmless. A commentary reports that people call Jinniu's carrying rice and dancing "pressing old-woman concern," then rejects their reading: it is "arsenic soaked in honey to entice people to put it in their mouths" (以蜜浸砒霜誘人下口). Elsewhere the location of Yaoshan's pressing concern is itself made the next interview question: "where is the place of his pressing old-woman concern?" (那裏是他老婆心切處). It can also enter verse, as in "pressing old-woman concern, laughing ha-ha, letting bystanders say long or short" (老婆心切呵呵笑，一任傍人說短長). Common frames include "only because" (the “only because” form, 24 occurrences; variant 祇為, 7) and "so very" (得恁麼老婆心切, 18). These uses support a forceful relational appraisal while preserving the possibility of criticism.

SearchAliases: an old woman's concern is pressing
Senses.Explanation: The phrase appraises urgently solicitous intervention: records sometimes praise it and sometimes compare it to poisoned honey. Literally, "an old woman's concern is pressing": old woman or granny (老婆) plus the concern being urgent or pressed hard (心切). The phrase is attested. It is a predicate applied to an unnamed interlocutor's insistent words or actions toward someone else, not the name of an inner state or a sentimental ideal. In the Linji–Huangbo–Dayu case, Dayu says Huangbo's old-woman concern was so pressing that "for you he exhausted himself completely" (為汝得徹困); when Linji returns, he says it was "only because the old-woman concern was pressing" (祇為老婆心切). In another exchange, a layman calls Huitang's concern pressing and Huitang replies, "I only want you to arrive home" (秖要公到家耳). The records thus show the idiom through predicates, agents, and replies rather than through a modern emotional gloss.

Senses.Explanation: Old-woman Chan is an appraisal label for talk or handling compared in the records with an old woman's solicitous speech. Masters apply it approvingly, critically, and ironically to sayings and encounters; it is not the name of a separate lineage. Dahui Zonggao asks whether the National Teacher's three calls may be called 'speaking old-woman Chan, dragging through mud and water' (說老婆禪拕泥帶水, ‘speaking old-woman Chan, dragging through mud and water’), and elsewhere says that if he had initially explained everything this way, the student would later have cursed him. Huang Yuangong's letter contrasts Miyun Yuanwu's 'pungent handling' (手段辛辣) with people elsewhere who speak old-woman Chan. The label is also attached to actual old-woman encounters in the Floating Cup and Mount Wutai cases. Dahui Zonggao calls a line 'old-woman Chan in the great Tang country' (大唐國裏老婆禪), and Wansong Xingxiu asks whether someone with firm heels would consent to learn old-woman Chan. The term is therefore an attested appraisal label rather than the name of a separate lineage: records apply it approvingly, critically, and ironically to different sayings and encounters.

Senses.Explanation: Laozi is the pre-Chan Chinese figure whom Chan records quote and place beside Confucius, Zhuangzi, and Gautama. Yongming Yanshou assigns Laozi to the ‘empty mystery’ in a threefold comparison; Fushi Tongxian and Guxue Zhenzhe juxtapose his ‘holding to the one’ with sayings of Confucius and Gautama. Yanxi Guangwen turns the story that Laozi transformed the foreigners into buddhas into a public question: why did he not transform them into Daoists? The Chan bend is not a new biography of Laozi but his use as a named voice and case figure within comparative instruction and teaching-seat questioning.

Senses.Explanation: As a productive noun or epithet, old fellow means an ‘old fellow’ and lets Chan speakers refer to teachers and case figures with striking familiarity. Nanyue Jiqi calls Xuefeng ‘this old fellow’ after raising his words; Dahui uses the same form for the named teaching figure in a self-narrated confrontation. Yinyuan asks who will vindicate ‘this old fellow,’ meaning Shakyamuni, while Zhean groups Dongshan, Shishuang, and Ming’an as ‘three old fellows.’ The Chan bend lies in this flexible familiarity: revered lineage and pre-lineage figures can be praised, tested, blamed, or handled as participants in a present public exchange rather than kept at ceremonial distance.

Senses.Explanation: 老師 designates or addresses a respected teacher or master. A preface calls Zibo Zhenke 達觀老師; Nanquan uses 王老師, ‘old Master Wang,’ for himself in separate encounters; and Dahui reports a dying official still calling out ‘Teacher!’ The word marks the speaker’s relation to, or respectful presentation of, the person named. It does not by itself prove dharma transmission or require the inflated English ‘venerable master.’

Poshan Haiming brushes off a question on the non-abiding mind by asking how one so old and great can still talk like this, Liangting Jingting rules that the sick old master misspoke to say someone might come see him, and Guantao Daqi grades Nanquan and Huangbo as two grand old men hindering each other.

Senses.Explanation: Xutang Zhiyu answers an unnamed questioner's claim that the moon is full in heaven but only half full among people with the blunt scene of an old crow pecking an oyster. The image refuses the questioner's polished moon comparison by replacing it with an awkward animal action. In a mid-autumn exchange, Xutang first calls talk of the moon at Vulture Peak and pointing at the moon at Caoxi deception; when the questioner offers his heaven-and-human contrast, Xutang replies only with the old crow pecking an oyster.

SearchAliases: a rat entering an ox horn
the rat driven into the ox horn
Zen a rat entering an ox horn
Senses.Explanation: A rat entering an ox horn is a narrowing image whose endpoints are stated differently in different passages. Dahui says to press inquiry until there is no further place to investigate, “like a rat entering an ox horn,” when the stealing mind suddenly ends. In a winter-solstice exchange, an unnamed monk asks how a patch-robed monk turns around when the yin forces are exhausted and one yang returns; Xutang Zhiyu answers with the phrase. Another instruction says to press forward day after day and month after month like the rat in the horn, and explicitly says that then a living road appears. The image can also be used as criticism: one record says that a declining lineage becomes narrower and narrower like the rat in the horn, while Ciming scolds an answer consisting of the phrase. These attested contrasts prevent the dictionary from turning the image into a fixed declaration of either hopeless dead end or guaranteed success. Chan makes the narrowing horn a public answer, an instruction, a rebuked reply, and an appraisal of a lineage's contraction. The exact phrase is attested in the corpus.
